items.title: The Bank of England announces that the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European…
items.snippet: The Bank of England announces that the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European hedgehog will feature on the next set of pound sterling notes to be issued in the United Kingdom. It will be the first time animals have replaced people on banknotes in England, which is intended to increase awareness of British wildlife.

items.title: The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper…
items.snippet: The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender.

items.title: Israel Police arrest 10 people in the occupied West Bank over attacks on American photojournalist Heidi…

items.title: South African police rescue about 200 people from an unregistered rehabilitation centre in Mpumalanga and…
items.snippet: South African police rescue about 200 people from an unregistered rehabilitation centre in Mpumalanga and arrest two people while investigating alleged kidnapping and health and safety violations. Fourteen people receive medical treatment following the rescue.

items.title: At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to…
items.snippet: At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027. To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed.

items.snippet: In women's rugby union, Canada defeats England 24–21 in a WXV Global Series match in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' four-year unbeaten run at 41 matches (the longest in rugby union history) after Shoshanah Seumanutafa scores a late try.

items.title: Protests continue for the second week in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, over water shortages and widespread…
items.snippet: Protests continue for the second week in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, over water shortages and widespread contamination. A study in June found that at least 93% of households' water systems contained no residual chlorine, but had elevated levels of lead, mercury, nitrates, and E. coli.
